Per-domain DNS management surfaced in admin UI and operations guide

nodes.label: JWT Bearer Authentication
nodes.rationale: Tokens include session_id, expire in 7 days, issued on register/login; used in Authorization header for protected endpoints.

nodes.label: SMTP Inbound Processing
nodes.rationale: Built-in SMTP server on port 25 accepts mail, stores parsed messages and attachments in DB, rejects RCPT for unknown addresses or inactive domains, extracts OTP via extractOtp, optionally posts to WEBHOOK_URL.

nodes.label: Socket.io Realtime Notifications
nodes.rationale: Clients emit 'subscribe' with address to join room inbox:<address>; server emits 'new-email' to that room when SMTP processing stores a mail.

nodes.label: Package Quota System
nodes.rationale: Address creation enforces package max_addresses quota from the packages table; package roles free|pro|pro_plus|admin.

nodes.label: Email Change Flow
nodes.rationale: Two-step request/confirm flow: request-email-change creates pending change and may email code if SMTP_RELAY configured; confirm-email-change completes with code.

nodes.label: API Key Authentication (tm_)
nodes.rationale: Automation uses tm_ API keys via X-Api-Key header (Bearer equivalent); web panel keeps JWT sessions. Keys carry per-key rate limits (standard 1000 req/min, master 10000 req/min), record usage count, last-used time, and IP; disabled/revoked keys return 401. Master key (tm_master_) has all scopes plus admin endpoints.

nodes.label: JSON Envelope Response Format
nodes.rationale: JSON responses use {success, data} or {success:false, error, message} envelope; attachments and SSE stream excluded since binary/stream. Mail list is a flat array inside data, not nested under an emails key.

nodes.label: Long-Poll Email Fetching
nodes.rationale: GET /emails/:address supports wait=0..30 (max 25s recommended), after_id for only-new records, since ISO-8601 timestamp, limit 1-100, order=desc|asc (default desc); received_at is UTC ISO-8601.

nodes.label: OTP Detection Scoring
nodes.rationale: otp_code persisted at SMTP receive. Detector scores subject, plain text, and HTML together; considers verification-label proximity, isolated code line, and source priority. Supports patterns like BXS-AJ2, ABC-123, IRU-VO0, 123456, 8492. Copyright years, dates/times, order/tracking/reference numbers are rejection signals. When an old mail is read, otp_code auto-corrects if a better code is found.

nodes.label: Per-Key Rate Limiting
nodes.rationale: Each key carries its own rate limit; standard users max 1,000 req/min, master keys max 10,000 req/min.

nodes.label: Mailbox Ownership Check
nodes.rationale: Address and mail endpoints enforce ownership: standard user keys manage only their own linked mailboxes; master key manages all mailboxes.

nodes.label: Basic Automation Flow
nodes.rationale: Canonical automation sequence: 1) list active domains via /addresses/domains?flat=1, 2) create address via POST /addresses (idempotent — returns existing mailbox if same address), 3) long-poll new mail via GET /emails/:address with wait=25.

nodes.label: Additive migration policy
nodes.rationale: Schema updates are additive migrations so existing user, address, mail and attachment data is never deleted; binary DB copy is taken for backup before stopping the service, and TEMPMAIL_DB_PATH allows verify/copy against a non-live DB.

nodes.label: Production env secret requirements
nodes.rationale: JWT_SECRET and ADMIN_PASSWORD must never ship to production with default values; API keys are stored in the DB only as SHA-256 hashes to limit leak impact.

nodes.label: Long-poll wait=25 over 2.5s short polling
nodes.rationale: Bots should use wait=25 long-polling or SSE instead of 2.5-second short polling because it reduces traffic and timeout probability.
